title: Python tests with unittest
when: The user wants tests for Python code using only the standard library, or a bug fix that needs a regression test.
prompt:
Goal: A unittest suite that runs with python -m unittest, covers edge cases, and isolates files, time and network.
Steps:
1. Create tests/__init__.py and tests/test_<module>.py importing the real code.
2. One TestCase class per unit (TestParsePrice) with test_<behavior> methods.
3. Cover normal input, boundaries, invalid input with assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx plus a check of str(ctx.exception), and one test per fixed bug.
4. Tables of cases with self.subTest(raw=raw) inside a loop.
5. Isolate with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() and addCleanup; patch time, environment and network with unittest.mock.patch.
6. Use assertEqual, assertAlmostEqual, assertIn, assertRegex so failures show values; run with python -m unittest discover -s tests -v.
Quality bar:
- Tests run in any order within seconds.
- One behavior per test.
- Nothing touches the real home folder or network.
Pitfalls:
- Methods without the test_ prefix that never run.
- Mocking the function under test.
- Exact equality on floats.
Verify:
- [ ] Files named test_*.py under tests/.
- [ ] Edge and error cases present.
- [ ] Temp resources cleaned up.
- [ ] No bare except.
Output: tests/test_*.py files and a Testing section in README.

examples.input: cria testes para a função que calcula frete
examples.output: tests/test_shipping.py with subTest table of weights, zero weight error, regression for rounding bug
